notes: dataset bhav:nifty-weekly (NSE F&O bhavcopy 2025-04-01..2026-10-28 + Angel NIFTY/INDIAVIX 5m); run by lab/_spreads.py, not the equity engine; option prices modelled (india-backtest/options.py), settlement real
rationale: On expiry day the whole time value of a Nifty weekly option goes to zero by 15:30. The buyers of cheap out-of-the-money expiry-day options are mostly individuals (SEBI's 2024 study: 91 % of individual F&O traders lose, most of them option buyers) paying a lottery premium for a large move in a few hours; the earlier backtest of that very trade (buy ATM on an ORB) lost 4 % of premium at mid prices on expiry days before costs. The mirror image, hedged: sell a vertical k x sigma away (sigma = India VIX scaled to the trading time left), long wing 100 points further, and let the exchange settle it. The 09:30 put spread harvests the index put skew (institutional hedging demand keeps puts dear); the ORB variant sells the side the first 15 minutes moved away from, so the seller takes the ORB buyer's side.
rules: Expiry day only, one trade. Entry at the close of the 09:30 bar (sell the PUT spread), or 'orb': at the first 5-minute close outside the 09:15-09:30 range by 14:30 (break up: sell the put spread; break down: sell the call spread). Short strike = the nearest 50-point strike at k_sigma x S x VIX/100 x sqrt(trading minutes to 15:30 / trading minutes in a year) from the spot; long wing 100 points further out. Fills at modelled mid -/+ 0.5 % (at least Rs 0.05) a leg; no stop; every leg held to the real settlement (bhavcopy intrinsic). One lot when 2 % exposure + 2 % expiry-day ELM per short leg + the maximum loss fits 90 % of Rs 1,00,000; else the day is skipped and counted.

author: strategy-researcher
notes: dataset bhav:nifty-weekly; run by lab/_spreads.py; entries modelled, daily marks and the exit at the real bhavcopy close
rationale: Volatility risk premium: Nifty weekly implied volatility sits above the volatility that is then realised, because hedgers roll weekly protection and directional retail buyers pay for convexity they rarely collect (SEBI 2024: 91 % of individual F&O traders lose). Theta is steepest in the last two sessions before expiry, so a condor opened then collects most of the week's premium in the least time. Closing at the real bhavcopy close of the session BEFORE expiry avoids expiry-day gamma, the unvalidated expiry-day model and SEBI's extra 2 % expiry-day ELM, which is what lets ONE condor lot fit a Rs 1,00,000 account. The 10:15 entry waits for the opening imbalance (overnight gap hedging) to settle before the strikes are chosen.
rules: On the session with dte trading days to the nearest NIFTY expiry (dte 2 = two sessions before; dte 1 = the session before), at the close of the 09:30 bar or of the 10:15 bar: sell the put spread and the call spread with short strikes at the nearest 50-point strike k_sigma x S x VIX/100 x sqrt(trading time to expiry / year) each side of the spot, long wings 100 points further out. Fills at modelled mid -/+ 0.5 % a leg (at least Rs 0.05). No stop. Marked daily at the real bhavcopy settle; closed at the real bhavcopy close of the session before expiry, each leg -/+ 0.5 % slippage. One position at a time, one lot when 2 % exposure per short leg + the maximum loss fits 90 % of Rs 1,00,000.

author: strategy-researcher

rationale: Buying the ATM Nifty weekly on a 15-minute opening-range break lost 4.2 % of premium at mid prices before costs (16 setups, a year), the worst on expiry days: most of that is the time value paid for a move that rarely comes, and the -25 % premium stop being hit by decay and noise. Selling an option 100-200 points further out against the long cuts the debit, and the short leg's own decay offsets part of the long's, so if the loss was mostly decay and spread the sign may flip; if the loss was the direction being wrong, a spread cannot fix it. The counterpart is the seller of the ATM option.
rules: Opening range = 09:15-09:30 high and low. The first 5-minute close above the high (by 14:30) buys the ATM call and sells the call `wing` points higher; below the low buys the ATM put and sells the put `wing` lower. Nearest expiry, expiry day included. Net debit sized at 20 % of Rs 1,00,000, whole lots. exit=stop_target: close when the spread's modelled value is 25 % under or 50 % over the debit; exit=flat: hold to 15:05 (15:00 on expiry day). Fills at modelled mid -/+ 0.5 % a leg. One trade a day.

notes: Pre-specified from Gao-Han-Li-Zhou 2018 before any look at the Angel data; creates the shared angel:nifty100:5m split
rationale: Gao, Han, Li and Zhou (2018, JFE) find that the first half-hour return of the market predicts the last half-hour return in the same direction, strongest on volatile and high-volume days. Mechanism: overnight news is absorbed by informed traders in the first 30 minutes, while a second group (late-informed investors, and institutions that execute 'at the close' or rebalance to the day's level) only trades towards the close, pushing prices the same way; on the other side are intraday liquidity providers who fade the morning move and unwind their inventory into the close. In India the F&O closing auction (since 2026-08-03) ends continuous trading at 15:15 for F&O stocks and our flat-by is 15:05, so the tradable 'last' window is 14:30 to 15:05, earlier than in the papers; the hypothesis is that the late-day flow already shows there.
rules: At the close of the 14:30 bar only. Signal = the NIFTY 50's first-half-hour return measured as in the paper, from the previous session's close to the 09:45 bar close (it includes the overnight gap), when signal=index, or the stock's own previous-close-to-09:45 return when signal=stock. If |signal| >= thr %: trade the stock in the signal's direction at the 14:30 close; stop 1.0 x the stock's 09:15-14:30 session range away (a disaster stop, the trade is a timed exit at flat-by 15:05); target 3 x the stop distance. One trade per stock per day.

author: strategy-researcher
notes: Angel frozen dataset 2025-04-01..2026-10-29; sector proxy = equal-weight NSE-industry peer basket inside the Nifty 100 (sector indices are not in ctx)
rationale: Sector-wide information (index futures flow, a macro print, a policy headline) is priced first in the sector's liquid names and the sector index futures; the less-watched members of the same NSE industry group adjust with a delay of minutes because their market makers re-quote slowly and retail attention arrives late (Lo-MacKinlay lead-lag; Hou 2007 industry information diffusion). A member that has not moved while most of its peers did should drift the sector's way over the next 15-60 minutes. Using the basket of peers rather than one leader filters single-stock news out of the signal: a trade needs at least two thirds of the peers moving the same way.
rules: From the bar closing 09:35 to 14:30, one trade per stock per day. Peers = the stock's NSE industry group inside the universe with a positive 20-session average traded value and bars at both ends of the window; at least 3 peers. Basket move = mean of the peers' 15-minute returns (close now vs close three bars earlier); at least two thirds of the peers must share its sign. Signal when |basket move| >= move_pct % and the stock's own 15-minute return is less than a third of it in the same direction. Long (basket up) at the close; stop = entry - 2 x ATR(14, 5-minute); target = entry + r x 2 x ATR. Mirror for a falling basket (short, stop above).

author: strategy-researcher
notes: intraday short-side family; frozen Angel dataset, offline
rationale: Breakout traders (and the stop orders of earlier shorts) buy the first close above the opening-range high. When the next bars close back INSIDE the range within 30 minutes, those buyers are under water with a stop just under the breakout bar; the first close back inside turns their buying into forced selling, while the earlier range low is the next cluster of stops. The other side is the momentum buyer who chased the breakout and must exit; the edge is paid for by his stop. The long ORB itself lost after charges on this universe, which is consistent with breakouts failing more often than not.
rules: Opening range = first or_minutes (15 or 30) of 5-minute bars from 09:15. A breakout = a bar closing above the range high (entries 09:30-14:30). The failure = the FIRST later bar (at most 6 bars = 30 minutes after the breakout) that closes back below the range high: sell at its close. Stop = the highest high since the breakout bar, at least 0.4 % above the entry (charges would eat a tighter stop). Target = r x the risk below the entry. If the failure comes more than 6 bars after the breakout, no trade that day. One trade per stock per day; covered by flat-by 15:05.

author: strategy-researcher
notes: intraday short-side family; frozen Angel dataset, offline
rationale: A single stock's break of its opening-range low is usually noise and gets bought back by VWAP and arbitrage desks. When the NIFTY 50 is itself below its VWAP (or under its own opening-range low) and the stock's sector peers are down from the open, the breakdown is part of an index-level sell programme (FPI basket selling, index-arbitrage unwind, ETF outflow) that is executed over hours, not minutes, so the move persists. The other side is the dip buyer who treats a sell programme as a stock-specific dip. Unconditioned, the short ORB was flat (-0.09R) on explore; the filter should remove the noise days.
rules: Opening range = first or_minutes (15 or 30) bars from 09:15. Sell at the close of the FIRST bar (09:30-14:30) that closes below the stock's range low AND, at that bar, NIFTY 50 is below its session VWAP (index_filter=vwap) or below its own opening-range low over the same minutes (index_filter=or_low) AND the equal-weight return of the stock's sector peers from their 09:15 open is negative. If an earlier bar already closed under the stock's range low, no trade that day. Stop = the range high (at least 0.4 % above the entry). Target = 2 x the risk. One trade per stock per day; covered by flat-by 15:05.

author: strategy-researcher
notes: intraday short-side family; frozen Angel dataset, offline
rationale: NSE's pre-open call auction and the first minutes are thin: overnight news and retail market orders set a gap-up open that is often more than the information warrants (over-reaction), and large caps have the depth for institutions to sell into it during the day. When the gap buyers cannot even hold the first 15-minute low, they are trapped above the market and their exits plus the gap-fill sellers push the price back toward the previous close. The other side is the retail trader who bought the gap at the open on the news. Gap fills are documented in US and Indian equities; the question is whether the net after Indian charges and slippage is positive on Nifty 100 names.
rules: Gap = the 09:15 bar's open over the previous session's close, at least gap_pct %. Opening range = the first 15 minutes (3 bars). Sell at the close of the FIRST bar closing 09:30-11:30 that closes below the 15-minute range low. Stop = the 15-minute range high (at least 0.4 % above the entry). Target: 'gapfill' = the previous close, only if it lies at least 0.8 x the risk below the entry (else no trade); '2r' = 2 x the risk below the entry. One trade per stock per day; covered by flat-by 15:05.

author: strategy-researcher
notes: intraday short-side family; frozen Angel dataset, offline
rationale: A stock that is down k x its daily ATR against its own sector peers by 10:15, and below its VWAP, is being sold on stock-specific information or flow (a downgrade, a block, a fund's exit) rather than with the market. Institutions split such orders over the session (VWAP / TWAP algos), so the underperformance continues into the afternoon: slow information diffusion plus persistent informed selling. The other side is the pairs / sector trader who buys the laggard expecting it to catch up with its peers, and the retail dip buyer. Short the stock only, not the spread (no hedge cost).
rules: At the bar closing 10:15 only: stock return = close / 09:15 open - 1; peer return = the mean of the same for the stock's sector peers in the universe (at least 2 peers). notes: 15 fixed same-industry pairs, each leg a separate engine trade (two sets of charges). Explore-only gross prototype: +0.02 pct of spread per pair-trade, so expected to fail on costs; logged to put real after-charge numbers on the pairs idea.
rationale: Two stocks in the same NSE industry share the sector's news and index flows; their intraday price ratio moves mostly because order flow hits one name first (a block in one, a basket order sized differently, a stop cascade in the more volatile leg). Arbitrage desks and the slower leg's own liquidity providers close the temporary divergence, so a ratio stretched two standard deviations from its recent intraday mean is expected to drift back. Trading both legs removes the market and sector direction; the bet is only on the relative mis-pricing.
rules: Fixed pairs inside one NSE industry: HDFCBANK/ICICIBANK, KOTAKBANK/AXISBANK, SBIN/BANKBARODA, BAJFINANCE/BAJAJFINSV, TCS/INFY, HCLTECH/WIPRO, NTPC/POWERGRID, TATAPOWER/ADANIPOWER, JSWSTEEL/TATASTEEL, HINDALCO/VEDL, SUNPHARMA/CIPLA, HINDUNILVR/ITC, BPCL/IOC, ULTRACEMCO/AMBUJACEM, MARUTI/M&M. rationale: The 15-minute ORB lost -0.10R gross / -0.33R net on the Nifty 50 (Yahoo, 60 days) and on the Tata group. The honest expectation is that most filters change little: the base rule's gross expectancy is negative and the filters are coarse.
rules: Base rule (orb15 default): opening range = high/low of the 09:15, 09:20, 09:25 bars. author: strategy-researcher
notes: Built after the explore-only measurement (scratch leadlag_measure.py): open laggards +15.7 bps/30 min at >=50 bps index move, t=1.2; the only sub-idea with gross mean above cost. 2 combos.
rationale: At the open the index level is set first: the pre-open auction, index futures and ETF/basket programs trade the index as a whole, while an individual large cap's first prints can be stale (thin auction, a few resting limit orders). Index futures lead cash stocks most at the open (Chan 1992; Lo-MacKinlay lead-lag). If NIFTY has moved at least thr % from its open by 09:30 and a constituent has moved less than a third of that, sector desks and arbitrageurs should re-quote the laggard towards the index over the next 30-60 minutes; the other side is the stale resting orders in the laggard's book. Explore measurement (angel:nifty100:5m explore, close-to-close): laggards after a >= 50 bps index move earned +15.7 bps in the next 30 min (n=458, day-clustered t=1.2), i.e. barely above the 10.4 bps cost.
rules: Only at the bar closing 09:30 (the third bar). Index move = NIFTY 09:30 close vs its 09:15 open; stock move = its 09:30 close vs its 09:15 open. Signal when |index move| >= thr % and the stock's signed move is below a third of the index move. Long (index up) at the close; stop = the low of the first three bars; target = entry + r x risk. Mirror for an index fall (short, stop = the high of the first three bars). Risk must be at least 0.2 % of the entry (tighter stops cost too much in R). One trade per stock per day.
